question: 66 women can do a piece of work in 79 days. Find the number of days required by 6 women to complete 1 / 11th of the work.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Using the chain rule formula: M₁ × D₁ × W₂ = M₂ × D₂ × W₁

⇒ 66 × 79 × (1 / 11) = 6 × D₂ × 1

⇒ 6 × 79 = 6 × D₂

⇒ D₂ = 79

**∴ The correct answer is 79 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number of women initially (M₁) = 66

Number of days taken initially (D₁) = 79

Number of women later (M₂) = 6

Work to be completed later = 1 / 11 of the total work

**Method Used:**

Total Work = Efficiency × Time (Assuming the efficiency of 1 woman is 1 unit/day)

 
 

 **Person**
 **Days**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 66 Women
 79
 5214
 66
 
 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total work completed by 66 women = 66 × 79 = 5214 units

⇒ Work to be completed by 6 women = 1 / 11 of Total work

⇒ Required work = 5214 ÷ 11 = 474 units

⇒ Efficiency of 6 women = 6 units/day

⇒ Number of days required = Required work ÷ Efficiency

⇒ Days = 474 ÷ 6 = 79

**∴ The correct answer is 79 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

MDH Rule (Chain Rule)

Used to compare two different groups working on a project: (M₁ × D₁ × H₁) / W₁ = (M₂ × D₂ × H₂) / W₂.

Work and Efficiency

Efficiency is inversely proportional to the time taken to complete a given amount of work. Total Work = Efficiency × Time.

Combined Work Rule

If person A takes x days and person B takes y days, their combined work per day is (1/x + 1/y).
